ai.description: *Cnemaspis kottiyoorensis* is a small gecko (34–36 mm SVL) with a brownish-grey body and yellow-spotted flanks. It is distinguished by a prominent precloacal pore and a distinct white vertebral stripe.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis kottiyoorensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on the throat, which is absent in most similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis kottiyoorensis* inhabits the moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found on rock surfaces at elevations of 300–800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kottiyoor day gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt for small insects on rocky surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis kottiyoorensis* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis kottiyoorensis* is endemic to the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at mid-elevations in the Kottiyoor region.
